name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset that connects language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations. It contains over 108,000 images with dense annotations of objects, attributes, and relationships within each image. Each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects. The dataset includes region descriptions, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs to enable modeling of relationships and comprehensive scene understanding.

rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. Images are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users, ranging from 72 to 1280 pixels wide with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images collected from the intersection of YFCC100M (Thomee et al., 2016) and MS-COCO (Lin et al., 2014) datasets. These are real-world photos collected from Flickr.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions: lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all attributes. For objects: Stanford NLP tools used to extract noun phrases automatically. For attributes: normalize based on morphology (stemming) and map to WordNet adjectives. For relationships: ignore all prepositions as they are not recognized by WordNet. All components canonicalized to WordNet synsets using most frequent matching synset according to WordNet lexeme counts, refined with hand-crafted mapping rules for common failure cases.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Region descriptions: Workers draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions, with BLEU score thresholds (0.7) enforced to ensure diversity. Objects: Extracted from descriptions by crowd workers who ground each object as a bounding box. Attributes and Relationships: Workers extract from region descriptions and connect objects with relationships. Scene graphs: Created by combining region graphs, merging co-referenced objects with 0.8 overlap threshold. Question-Answer pairs: Workers write pairs following rules to start with one of seven Ws (who, what, where, when, why, how, which), avoid ambiguous questions, and be precise. Two types collected: freeform QAs (8 pairs per image) and region-based QAs (based on given regions).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All data go through verification stage using two strategies: majority voting (three unique workers vote on correctness, annotation added if at least two verify) and rapid judgments (for objects only, using interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing). Canonicalization mappings verified by workers who confirm or change mappings from top four alternative synsets.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. For verification, three unique workers vote on each annotation (majority voting).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Geographic distribution: 93.02% from United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% others. Age distribution: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest 18 years old, oldest 68 years old. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. Workers achieved 94.1% retention rate.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (Manning et al., 2014) used to extract noun phrases automatically from region descriptions and QAs. Stanford dependency parser used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions to speed up object extraction. VGG 16-layer network (Simonyan and Zisserman, 2014) used for feature extraction in experiments.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images contain people and may capture human attributes such as age, gender, and activities. Annotator demographics collected include age, gender, and geographic location.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets show (e.g., ski, ballplayer, racket referring to images of people playing sports). Images from Flickr may reflect biases in what users choose to photograph and upload. Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to bias in image sources.
rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. WordNet's frequency counts prefer abstract senses of words over spatial senses present in visual data. The model's lower representation of concrete or spatial senses required hand-crafted rules to address common failure cases. Relationship prediction experiments show high intra-class variability making relationships not visually distinct enough for discriminative models to learn effectively. Current models fail to describe all different events captured in an image and provide only high-level summaries.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking for comprehensive scene understanding tasks including: attribute prediction, relationship prediction, dense image captioning, visual question answering, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, semantic image retrieval. The dataset enables modeling of relationships between objects and supports both perceptual and cognitive computer vision tasks.
